questions.text:
Consider 4-variable functions [latex] f 1, f 2, f 3, f 4 [/latex] expressed in sum-of-minterms form as given below.
[latex] \begin{aligned} & f 1=\sum(0,2,3,5,7,8,11,13) \\ & f 2=\sum(1,3,5,7,11,13,15) \\ & f 3=\sum(0,1,4,11) \\ & f 4=\sum(0,2,6,13) \end{aligned} [/latex]


With respect to the circuit given above, which of the following options is/are CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Compute the AND, OR and XOR outputs as minterm sets:
- AND: [latex]f_1\cdot f_2[/latex] = common minterms = [latex]\{3,5,7,11,13\}[/latex]
- OR: [latex]f_3+f_4=\{0,1,4,11\}\cup\{0,2,6,13\}=\{0,1,2,4,6,11,13\}[/latex]
- XOR keeps minterms present in exactly one of them: [latex]\{3,5,7\}\cup\{0,1,2,4,6\}[/latex]; 11 and 13 are in both, so they drop.

[latex]Y=\Sigma(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7)=\Pi(8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15)[/latex] (i.e. [latex]Y=\bar A[/latex]).

Answer: [latex]Y=\Sigma(0,\ldots,7)[/latex] and [latex]Y=\Pi(8,\ldots,15)[/latex]

questions.text: Which of the following is/are EQUAL to 224 in radix-5 (i.e., base-5) notation?
questions.solution:
[latex](224)_5=2\times25+2\times5+4=64[/latex]

- [latex](64)_{10}=64[/latex] True
- [latex](100)_8=64[/latex] True
- [latex](50)_{16}=80[/latex] False
- [latex](121)_7=49+14+1=64[/latex] True

Answer: 64 in radix-10, 100 in radix-8, 121 in radix-7

questions.text: For a Boolean variable [latex]x[/latex], which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]x\cdot1=x[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE (identity).
- [latex]x+1=x[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE, since [latex]x+1=1[/latex].
- [latex]x\cdot x=0[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE, since [latex]x\cdot x=x[/latex] (idempotence).
- [latex]x+\bar{x}=1[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE (complement).

Answer: [latex]x+1=x[/latex] and [latex]x.x=0[/latex]

questions.text:
The format of a single-precision floating-point number as per the IEEE 754 standard is:

Choose the largest floating-point number among the following options.
questions.solution:
In IEEE 754, an exponent of all 1s (255) is reserved for [latex]\infty[/latex]/NaN.

- (A): exponent 127 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]1.11\ldots1\times2^{0}\approx2[/latex]
- (B): exponent [latex]11111110=254[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]1.11\ldots1\times2^{127}\approx2^{128}[/latex], the largest finite number
- (C): exponent 255 with non-zero mantissa [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] NaN, not a number at all
- (D): [latex]1.0\times2^0=1[/latex]

Answer: B

questions.text:
Consider a digital logic circuit consisting of three 2-to-1 multiplexers M1, M2, and M3 as shown below. [latex] X 1 [/latex] and [latex] X 2 [/latex] are inputs of [latex] M 1 [/latex]. [latex] X 3 [/latex] and [latex] X 4 [/latex] are inputs of [latex] M 2 [/latex]. [latex] A, B [/latex], and [latex] C [/latex] are select lines of [latex] M 1, M 2 [/latex], and [latex] M 3 [/latex], respectively.

For an instance of inputs [latex] X \mathbf{X l}=\mathbf{X} \mathbf{2}=\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{X} 3=\mathbf{0} [/latex], and [latex] \mathrm{X} 4=\mathbf{0} [/latex], the number of combinations of [latex] A, B, C [/latex] that give the output [latex] Y=1 [/latex] is _____
questions.solution:
Look at each multiplexer separately:
- M1: both inputs [latex]X1=X2=1[/latex], so [latex]Q1=1[/latex] whatever A is.
- M2: both inputs [latex]X3=X4=0[/latex], so [latex]Q2=0[/latex] whatever B is.
- M3: [latex]Y=Q1=1[/latex] when [latex]C=0[/latex], and [latex]Y=Q2=0[/latex] when [latex]C=1[/latex].

So [latex]Y=1[/latex] exactly when [latex]C=0[/latex]; A and B are free: [latex]2\times2=4[/latex] combinations.

Answer: 4
